rationale: A macro in TYPE position must not be published as a member name. `c/macro-generated-field` (#928) already rules and pins the ADJACENT shape: when the macro OWNS the name (`BIT(closing);`) there is no declarator, `fieldDeclarationHasDeclarator` refuses, and silence is correct. This is the shape that test cannot see. `git_array_t(size_t) line_index;` parses as `macro_type_specifier` + a SIBLING `field_identifier`, so a declarator IS present and the #928 refusal does not fire -- but the extractor's per-child loop treats every child that is not a type node as a DECLARATOR, and a `macro_type_specifier` was in neither the type list nor the skip list, so it was descended for its identifier and published BESIDE the real member. Measured over the four declared corpora (3,997 files): 60 phantom `contains` edges, 48 of them beside the correct member, across 19 macro names -- git_array_t x13 (libgit2), ql_elm x11 / ql_head x5 / rb_node x5 (jemalloc), STACK_OF (curl), HRESULT and ULONG (libgit2's winhttp header), GIT_ALIGN, plus C++-header debris (noexcept, decltype, operator) that tree-sitter-c parses out of libstdc++/libc++. clang, a different parser, independently reports them as PHANTOM members. This is the #928 defect verbatim -- a member named after a name no C declaration in the file gives to any member -- and it is NOT C-D2: the real member is in the parse and was already published, so only the duplicate is removed. The forbid rows are the phantoms; the expect rows are the real members beside them, which is the control that this is a duplicate being dropped rather than a member being lost.
